notes: Calibration status: written against the plan of Главы 1–5 (content/ru/plan/chapters.json). Writers imitate its density, repetition sources (rule of three in the dictation, the что?/кого? question chain, the four-line tableau), gloss economy, Pensa and exercise shapes; they never copy its sentences.

Licensing self-check: every token checked with pymorphy3 against the cumulative plan lexicon and grammar-map.json through G06 (scratch simulator); the remaining licensed-incidental forms are the G05 imperative chunks (Чита́йте, Чита́й, пиши́) and the 1pl classroom commands (Пи́шем!, Повторя́ем!).
Present-tense narration (before Глава 10). No dative except the baseline-licensed тебе́ (Тебе́ легко́); no instrumental; locatives only in -е (в окне́, в шко́ле, на доске́, на уро́ке, в избе́).
The proverb in words_with_history is a quotation (уче́нье, свет, тьма are not course lexemes); it is a margin box, glossed by its context, never tested.

Assumption flagged for the integrator: segment 'tableau' marks the four-line dictation tableau (the Welsh Mae-run exemption) although Russian has no Mae ratio; it documents the deliberate parallel structure.
Pilot revision (2026-10-18, after Главы 1–5 were written): segment IDs kept; new segments get new IDs (s130 onwards) and are inserted in reading order.

Continuity with Главы 1–5: Ivan works in the field in the morning and goes to school in the evening, as he told his father in Глава 5 («А ве́чером — шко́ла»); the school map of Глава 5 hangs there and, as in Глава 1, Берёзовка is not on it, but Ivan knows where it is; Шарик sleeps in the yard (Глава 2) and Ivan keeps the mended slate from him («Нет, Ша́рик, э́то не твоя́ доска́!», a callback to Дед's «Ша́рик, э́то твоя́ доска́?»).
Two planner pins corrected: «большо́й» in s012 and s024 is nominative masculine, not genitive feminine.

Inductive-clarity pass (2026-10-19, brief ru-fix-brief.md): every sentence anchored by known Russian, an adjacent contrast, a rendered vignette/diagram or a Russian gloss; drills cut to 3 per section of 5–6 items and reordered so no drill uses a word, form or character before the story shows it. New segments s135, s140, s141, s143; s002, s128, s131 deleted; s032–s033 moved after the laughter so ти́хо follows гро́мко.

Fix pass after the Codex critique (2026-10-19): ста́ршего бра́та, молоду́ю учи́тельницу and учи́тельницу shown in the story before they are drilled; verb and adjective drills and their Образцы limited to demonstrated forms; отца́/сестру́/ждём/на́шего items replaced; priest identified by vignette and «его́ рабо́та — це́рковь»; легко́ glossed beside s067; «Непра́вильно. Ещё раз!»; «На э́той ка́рте Берёзовки нет» (the classroom map is not the book's map); s135 cut for length; s144 added. The priest vignette media/vignettes/ru-mir-01-l06-img-batyushka.svg is referenced with status planned until the file lands; flip it to draft then. «На э́той ка́рте» was tried and dropped: the adjectival locative is unlicensed before G07, so s134 says «На ка́рте шко́лы».

review_questions.question: Slate vs blackboard: both are «доска́» here (Nastya's slate, the school board). Is the double use clear and period-correct (а́спидная доска́ for the slate)?
«уже́ лежа́т» for 'have already gone to bed' (спать is not yet a lexeme): natural enough, or does it read as 'are lying ill'?
Is the elliptical «Но уже́ не о́чень» natural narration?
Would a village priest of 1913 say «Ты гра́мотный?» to a peasant of 19? (Register check: ты from priest to parishioner assumed.)
[?] The wall map in a village zemstvo school of 1913 (plausible; a museum zemstvo school in Konstantinovo shows an 1895 map) is not documented in the history notes.

words_with_history.title: Слова́ с исто́рией
text: Ве́ра Никола́евна говори́т «гра́мота» и ду́мает: бу́квы, слова́, страна́ Росси́я.
А Ива́н говори́т «гра́мота» и ду́мает: моё и́мя, моя́ дере́вня, моя́ рука́.
words_with_history.note_en: In 1897 about a fifth of the Empire's people could read; by 1913 about three army recruits in four were at least semi-literate. Some zemstvo schools also taught adults in the evening. Gramota also meant a charter or official paper; the proverb says 'learning is light, ignorance is darkness'.

grammar.title: Кого́? Что?
grammar.rule: Ива́н → Ива́на, брат → бра́та, ба́тюшка → ба́тюшку · стол → стол, окно́ → окно́ · он → его́, она́ → её
grammar.note_en: In the singular, masculine nouns for people and animals (except those in -а/-я) take the genitive form as objects: Ива́на, бра́та, Ша́рика. Masculine and neuter nouns for things stay unchanged (стол, окно́). Every noun in -а/-я, masculine or feminine, animate or not, takes -у/-ю (ба́тюшку, Ва́ню, Ве́ру, ла́мпу). Adjectives follow: но́вого ученика́. Object pronouns usually precede the verb: Я тебя́ зна́ю.
